chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries off his son while he is young (a minor). He said: 'If the son has wealth, the dowry is upon him. And if the son does not have wealth, the father is liable for the dowry; whether he assumed liability or not.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the dowry if a minor son gets married?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of paternal guarantee (kafalah) in marriage contracts for minors, ensuring the bride's financial rights are secured even if the son lacks independent wealth. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the father acts as the legal guardian and financial surety, emphasizing the protection of the bride's mahr as a mandatory right rather than a discretionary gift.
